items.text: Reductions: localise on $S$ (affine $S_i$), then on $X=\bigcup X_i$, $Y=\bigcup Y_j$.
Z=X\times_SY\supset Z_{ij}=X_i\times_SY_j,\qquad Z_{ij}\hookrightarrow Z\ \text{open immersions},\ \ Z=\sup Z_{ij}
Fibre $X_s\to X$: injective, with the induced topology.
Infinite inverse limits of schemes affine over $S$
Products $\leftrightarrow$ (infinite) tensor products; kernels $\leftrightarrow$ cokernels; filtering inverse limits $\leftrightarrow$ filtering direct limits (quasi-coherent).
X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A\ \text{affine over }S,\ Z/S\ \text{any scheme}:\qquad \operatorname{Hom}_S(Z,X)\ \simeq\ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_S\text{-alg}}(\mathcal A,g_*\mathcal O_Z)
The same functors are represented in the larger category of locally ringed spaces (a morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a homomorphism $A\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$).

Grassmannian bundle: quotients (or submodules) of $\mathcal M$ locally free of a given rank; flag bundles: $\mathcal M\supset\mathcal M_1\supset\mathcal M_2\supset\cdots$ with prescribed ranks of the quotients.
Local structure: localisation of a scheme at a point
$\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to X$ is a monomorphism and a homeomorphism onto its image (induced topology).
The closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a specialisation of all its points; their images are generalisations of $x$.
